content:
As previously announced earlier this year, the Google Chrome browser has now adopted a two-week update cycle.

Previously, Chrome released a major "milestone" update every four weeks, such as upgrading from version 100 to version 101. Before 2021, Google used a six-week cycle.

The purpose of releasing major updates every two weeks is to more quickly provide "new features, performance improvements, and bug fixes." Each update will contain less content, but the frequency of updates will increase accordingly.

On the other hand, Google stated that this "accelerated update cadence is good news for the entire web." Developers will be able to "roll out modern web features with greater confidence, as the deployment window is tighter, interoperability updates arrive faster, and security improvements can reach users across platforms more quickly." The fact that each release has a "smaller scope" will make "regression issues easier to pinpoint."

In terms of security, Google pointed out that with the rise of AI, this change helps to "respond to rapidly evolving threats."

For enterprise customers, Chrome offers an "Extended Stable" channel that updates every eight weeks: version 156 will be released first, followed by version 160. Google noted that most enterprise users should adopt the Stable version, which updates every two weeks.

Chrome 153 is rolling out to desktop, Android, and iOS platforms starting today. Meanwhile, version 154 will be released on September 22.
